findings.title: Read-only group permission grants top-level group management
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() relies on this method through requireManage(), so an administrator granted only VIEW can create groups or move existing subgroups to the top level. This crosses the read/write authorization boundary. Only the MANAGE scope should satisfy this check.

findings.title: Use model group IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
findings.body: groupResource.getId() identifies an authorization resource, not a GroupModel; AdminPermissionsSchema stores the model group ID in the resource name. Passing the authorization ID to hasPermission() makes its findByName() lookup miss and fall back to the all-groups permission. Returning that ID also supplies invalid group IDs to user search and count queries. In particular, an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant adds the aggregate authorization resource's UUID to the membership filter, causing searches and counts to return no matching users. Resolve actual group IDs and handle the aggregate resource separately.

findings.title: Assign the Groups type to individual group authorization resources
findings.body: The new group resolution path creates an authorization resource named after the group ID but never assigns it the Groups resource type. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() exclusively enumerates resources through findByType(..., "Groups", ...), so these individual resources are omitted. Consequently, a group-specific VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grant can authorize direct user access but contributes no IDs to /users/count or pre-pagination user search filtering, producing incorrect counts and incomplete pages. Individual group resources need a matching type or a different enumeration mechanism.

findings.title: Allow the group-member creation fallback with FGAP V2
findings.body: canCreateGroupMembers() still returns false unless the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled. With V2 selected, that V1 feature check is false, so an administrator granted MANAGE_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP on a group cannot create a user in that group: createUser() rethrows the failed global manage-users authorization as HTTP 403 without evaluating the group grants. Update this guard to support V2 so the newly implemented group scopes work through the existing member-creation path.
